# lottie-render

> An MIT-licensed Lottie JSON to MP4 converter. Use the browser demo, Node.js library, CLI, or self-hosted HTTP API.

The demo previews JSON locally in a sandboxed browser frame. Only clicking Convert to MP4 uploads the file. Chromium renders frames on the server, and FFmpeg encodes a silent H.264 MP4 with a white background. Demo conversion resamples frames to preserve timing. It does not export alpha transparency or audio. Temporary render files are deleted after transfer or failure.

Upload size, source duration, dimensions, and concurrency are capped. See the demo page or /api/config for this deployment's current limits. Use self-contained JSON with embedded assets. External network assets are blocked; evaluated expressions are also blocked in the local preview. Self-hosting requires Node.js, Playwright's Chromium and FFmpeg, or Docker.

## Documentation

- [Source and quick start](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render): Project source and usage.
- [Library API](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/docs/api.md): Render options and result types.
- [HTTP API](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/docs/http-api.md): Upload endpoint and response metadata.
- [Self-hosting](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/docs/demo.md): Demo configuration and resource limits.
- [中文文档](https://github.com/steven-panxd/lottie-render/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md): Chinese quick start.
